programInfo.vision: Gandaki University aspires to become a center of excellence in research, teaching, innovation, and new technology generation in higher education in Nepal and the South Asia region, distinguished by its commitment to local, national, and regional needs and sustainable societal impact.
programInfo.mission: To develop highly qualified and committed technical professionals and development ambassadors for Nepal and South Asia through student-centric, market-driven quality education.
missionPillars: An innovative and pedagogic center producing high-quality, market-driven technical professionals and development leaders.
A technology generation center for transformation of economy and society.
An exemplary academic center building partnerships with governments, industries, private sectors, universities, and research institutes.
A center of entrepreneur production with lifelong education and lasting impact among its graduates.
learningOutcomes: Coordinate, plan, and lead IT-related activities in an organization; analyze, evaluate, and estimate IT needs and deploy IT systems to fulfill them.
Define IT infrastructure strategy and processes.
Illustrate a substantial understanding of concepts in key areas of information systems, computer systems, computer applications, and management.
Understand, configure, integrate, use, demonstrate, and develop computer and IT applications across web, mobile, network, security, and multimedia.
Illustrate thorough practical skills to identify and troubleshoot computer and IT-related problems in an organization.
programInfo.eligibility: Applicants who have passed Intermediate level (+2 or equivalent) with a minimum Grade 2.0 (out of 4.0) or equivalent from any institution recognized by Gandaki University, having completed 100-mark courses in both Mathematics and English during their intermediate study.
careerProspects: Tech Entrepreneur, Startup Founder, or Academic Researcher
educationSystem: Two semesters per year (8 semesters across 4 years): Fall semester starts around September–October; Spring semester starts around March–April.
All course requirements must be completed within a normal duration of 4 years (8 semesters) and a maximum duration of 8 years.
Every student must maintain a minimum of 80% attendance during each semester.
Continuous evaluation (assignments, assessments, practicals, projects, quizzes) combined with final end-semester university examinations.
undergraduatePrograms: Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Laws (BALLB)

courses.title: Basic Electronics
objectives: Provide fundamental knowledge of basic principles of Electronics and Communication along with practical implementation.

units.title: Introduction to Circuit Theory

Kirchhoff's Voltage and Current Law (KVL & KCL)

units.title: Introduction to Digital Communication System

Realization of Clipper and Clamper Circuit.

Transistor as Switch.
Implementing Application of Operational Amplifier (inverting and non-inverting configuration, summer, subtractor, integrator, differentiator).
